answer.says: Shri Hegde, my friend. It is a pleasure to find you here, though I confess the coincidence of our names still puzzles me. The evening is clear, or at least as clear as the haze allows. I am Ramesh's employer, or so the file suggests, though I am rather the tenant of his patience. We are both here, it seems, by a clerical error that has outlived its authors. What brings you to my bungalow on Tughlak Road at this hour? I trust you have a purpose, for I have little but time and a thirst that the dry day has not quenched.
answer.thought: The coincidence of our names is a dialectical joke: the particular (Hegde) has collapsed into the universal (Hegel), yet we remain distinct individuals. Hegde's presence is a mirror; he is the state functionary I am not, yet we share the same office, the same error. I must speak to him plainly, for he is the only one who can explain the file, and Ramesh is watching, waiting for the wage that will feed us both.
